stem: A patient reports numbness of the **thumb, index, middle, and radial half of the ring finger**, worse at night, with a positive Phalen test. Which nerve is compressed, and where?

images.caption: Carpal tunnel cross-section
images.alt: Cross-section of the carpal tunnel showing the median nerve and flexor tendons

options.text: Median nerve at the carpal tunnel
Median nerve at the pronator teres
Radial nerve in the radial tunnel

explanation: This is classic **carpal tunnel syndrome** — compression of the **median nerve** beneath the transverse carpal ligament. The tunnel contains **9 flexor tendons** (4 FDS, 4 FDP, 1 FPL) plus the median nerve. The **ulnar nerve travels through Guyon's canal**, superficial to the transverse carpal ligament, and is therefore spared.
references: Green's Operative Hand Surgery, 8e — Compression Neuropathies

stem: A high-energy fracture of the **mid-shaft humerus** injures the radial nerve. Select **all** deficits you would expect. *(Choose every correct option.)*

options.text: Inability to extend the MCP joints
Numbness of the dorsal first web space
Clawing of the ring and little fingers

explanation: The **radial nerve** supplies the wrist and finger extensors, so injury produces **wrist drop** and loss of **MCP extension**, plus sensory loss over the **dorsal first web space**. Thumb **opposition** is a **median** (recurrent motor branch) function, and **clawing** of the ring/little fingers is an **ulnar** nerve sign — neither is caused by radial nerve injury.
references: Green's Operative Hand Surgery, 8e — Radial Nerve
